title: Corryhabbie Hills Circuit
summary: A suggested broad moorland round above Glenfiddich with a mix of open hill, estate track help, and several named tops. This is not a precision nav product — it’s a practical route idea to sanity-check on the drive up.
disclaimer: Suggested route only. Built from map screenshots and rough grid-ref anchors. Not gospel, not a precision navigation product, and not a substitute for proper hill judgement on the day.
parkingNote: Start / parking around NJ 27613 30622 near Ellivreid. Park considerately — don’t block gates, farm access, or anything that might need a tractor later.

routeOptions.name: Full round
routeOptions.reason: Better overall route shape and fuller day out.
suggestedLine: Descent choice / zig-zag track ref — NJ 28983 28035
Central return corridor / Folds of Corhabbie side
routeOptions.explanation: Gets the awkward lower western ground done early, sweeps the main hill mass in a sensible order, and keeps the cleaner track-assisted return for later in the day. Better if the weather is decent and the group wants a proper full outing.

routeOptions.name: Looser / easier day
routeOptions.reason: Better if the vibe is more relaxed and social.
suggestedLine: Descent choice / zig-zag track ref — NJ 28983 28035
routeOptions.explanation: Hits the best-feeling tops without dragging every side lump into it. More flexible, easier to shorten, and more realistic for a late-start social hill day.

recommendation: Option A is the better route.
Option B is probably the better hang.
goodStopSpots: Corryhabbie Hill for the biggest-feeling perch.
Muckle Lapprach shoulder for a decent sit-down spot.
Track junction near NJ 28983 28035 as an easy regroup point.
terrainVibe: Expect broad open hill, a few heathery and probably soggy bits, and enough track options to stop it turning into total nonsense. No real technical ground — just route choices and how much nonsense you want to voluntarily add.
wildlifeTexture: Heather, blaeberry, bog moss, wetter peaty ground, likely red grouse, deer, meadow pipits, and maybe something decent overhead if luck is in.
